messages:
Sam: Quick question — who owns the routing decision surface for model routing? console policy layer, control-plane service, or the edge gateway? thinking about canaries + quota enforcement.
Maria: my vote is control-plane for the canonical policy. console just edits the policy, gateway enforces. keeps runtime simple. :+1:
Tony: +1 to CP canonical but want the console UX to show live impact (preview + impact estimate). product needs a canary toggle that's easy to revert. Lina can speak to UX.
Lina: Yup, from product POV we need a one-click canary with a rollback button and visible metrics (latency, errors, cost delta). If it's in the control plane we can surface the rollout state.
Kai: Couple constraints: gateway needs low-latency lookups. If control-plane is the source of truth we need a local cache + streaming updates to avoid per-request RPC. Also think about partial failures -> gateway should have fallback policy.
Maria: Agreed. implementation idea: policy published to a versioned blob in S3-like store + gateway subscribes to changes via watch stream. gateways keep in-memory eval.
Sam: Does anyone worry about consistency windows during rollout? e.g., canary hits 5% but some gateways still on old policy for a few seconds -> weird split behavior.
Tony: That's fine if we expose it to users. But for weirdness mitigation we should do rollout by shard key (tenant or model-id) not random per-request. deterministic hashing reduces split exposure.
Kai: Exactly — shard-based sampling: hash(tenant_id) % 100 < N gives stable canary. Implemented at gateway local eval level.
Maria: Also need audit trails: who changed the policy, diff viewer. Control-plane already has these hooks so win.
Sam: What about quotas? Should quota enforcement be at gateway or centralized?
Kai: Enforce locally for speed but keep central counters for billing and global limits. Use local token-bucket with occasional reconciliation.
Lina: Telemetry needs: per-route token usage, canary vs stable traces, and a cost-per-token projection widget in console.
Tony: For rollout UX, we can show a simulated traffic sample in console that runs the policy logic against recent traffic to estimate impact before applying.
Maria: That simulation needs access to the same feature set as gateway eval (headers, model metadata). So we should standardize the policy language (simple DSL or protobuf schema) and a shared evaluator lib used by console (sim), control-plane (publish), and gateway (runtime).
Sam: Policy language debate: full protobuf message matchers vs small declarative DSL. Thoughts?
Kai: Keep it declarative and small. Protobuf matchers are powerful but risk versioning footguns. DSL compiled to proto for runtime is okay.
Maria: +1 DSL compiled to proto. That way we can evolve under the hood but keep UX simple.
Tony: Also need feature flags per-policy (enable/disable automatic fallback to lower-cost model on high latency). Might be richer than basic routing.
Lina: Important: make the console defaults safe. e.g., new policy auto-rolled to 0% unless user explicitly increases. Also require a preflight sim.
Sam: Ops question: how do we debug policy mismatches at runtime? gateway should expose current policy version and last update ts in response headers.
Kai: yep add headers: X-Policy-Version, X-Policy-Source, and maybe X-Policy-Hash. We'll log policy decision traces to tracing system when debug flag set.
Maria: Also tie policy rollout changes to alerts if error rate or tail latency for affected routes increases > threshold. Control-plane emits rollout events to alerting.
Sam: Any strong objections to this architecture: CP canonical policy (versioned blob + audit), gateway local eval w/ streaming updates, console owning UX + simulation, quotas local token-bucket + central reconciliation, deterministic shard canaries?
Tony: No objections. Only asks: document the DSL and provide a reference evaluator in Go + TS so console and gateway share semantics.
Kai: I'll prototype the streaming update proto + header bits. infra-bot: scheduled CI job created for policy-eval lib spike (#1234).
Lina: I'll put a short wireframe for canary UX in Figma and share.
Sam: Cool. Action items: Kai protos + gateway patch, Tony + Maria to draft DSL, Lina to do UX mock, Sam to write RFC. Back in a week? :rocket:
